ISO 6346 is the international standard for container identification. It sets the owner code, the equipment category letter, the six-digit serial number, the check digit and the size and type code.
How is the check digit worked out?

Each of the first ten characters gets a value (letters have values from 10 up, skipping multiples of 11). Each value is multiplied by 2 to the power of its position (1, 2, 4, 8 and so on), the results are added, divided by 11, and the remainder (with 10 counted as 0) is the check digit.
What does the fourth letter mean?

It is the equipment category. U is a freight container, J is detachable freight-container related equipment such as a generator set, and Z is a trailer or chassis. Almost every container you handle ends its prefix in U.
The check digit is wrong. What now?

Most often it is a typo or a misread character, such as O for 0 or I for 1. Check the number on the container door and on the booking or bill of lading. If it still fails, ask the shipping line before you file the document.
Does a valid check digit mean the container exists?
No. It only means the number is correctly formed. Only the shipping line or the container owner can tell you if that box is real and which booking it belongs to.
Need the container tracked, or the shipment cleared? Talk to a licensed customs broker.
